quarterly_data.signal: GlobalFoundries 20-F customer concentration: Customer A amounted to 16.4% of total wafer revenue in 2025 (15.7% in 2024, 17.0% in 2023); Customer C amounted to 13.9% in 2025 (less than 10% in 2024 and 2023); Customer B was less than 10% in 2025 (10.7% in 2024). GF's ten largest customers accounted for approximately 63% of its wafer shipment volume in 2025 (65% in 2024, 72% in 2023). Customers are not named.
quarterly_data.figure: Customer A 16.4%; Customer C 13.9% of wafer revenue; top ten ~63% of wafer shipment volume (2025)

quarterly_data.signal: GlobalFoundries 20-F long-term agreements: as of December 31, 2025 the aggregate remaining revenue commitment reflected by LTAs was approximately $11 billion - binding, multi-year, reciprocal minimum purchase and supply commitments, many including customer advance payments and capacity reservation fees to secure future supply. 51.8% of these remaining performance obligations is expected to be recognized in the next 24 months and the remaining 48.2% substantially within the following three years. GF also said that, in light of current demand dynamics, its ability to enter into LTAs has diminished and its commercial focus has shifted to a wider funnel aimed at single-sourced design wins; single-sourced business was approximately 63% of 2025 wafer shipment volume.
quarterly_data.figure: LTA remaining revenue commitment ~$11 billion; 51.8% within 24 months; single-sourced ~63% of wafer volume

quarterly_data.signal: GlobalFoundries 20-F capex and capacity: capital expenditures (property, plant and equipment, intangible assets and capitalized development costs) were $722 million in 2025, $625 million in 2024 and $1.804 billion in 2023. As of December 31, 2025 GF had $800 million of purchase commitments related to contracts for capital expenditures, $619 million of it due within 12 months. Its CHIPS Act Direct Funding Agreement (up to $1.5 billion, plus $75 million added in January 2025 for a new center for advanced packaging and testing at the Fab 8 facility) supports expanding Fab 8 in Malta, New York, a new fab on the Fab 8 campus and modernizing Fab 9 in Burlington, Vermont; GF received funding for the first two Fab 8 expansion milestones in 2025. Through a strategic partnership with a China-based foundry, GF is proceeding with plans to let customers access GF production to serve domestic Chinese demand.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 capex $722 million; capex purchase commitments $800 million ($619 million within 12 months)

quarterly_data.signal: GlobalFoundries 20-F full-year 2025 revenue split: wafer revenue $6,022 million (XBRL: -1.2% YoY), about 89% of net revenue, and non-wafer revenue $769 million (+17.9%); communications infrastructure & data center revenue was $745 million versus $577 million in 2024. IFRS gross margin was 24.9% versus 24.5%, driven by improved factory loading and lower factory spending, partially offset by reduced customer underutilization payments and capacity reservation fees and a decline in ASPs.
quarterly_data.figure: wafer revenue $6,022 million; non-wafer $769 million (+17.9%); CID $745 million; IFRS gross margin 24.9%

quarterly_data.signal: GlobalFoundries 20-F: GF has entered into patent cross-licenses with a number of leading advanced semiconductor companies, including AMD, Samsung, TSMC and IBM, which it says provide freedom of operation under patents owned or subsequently divested by those companies.

contracts.signal: GlobalFoundries 20-F: Soitec is GF's primary supplier of 300mm SOI wafers and accounted for approximately 71% of GF's SOI wafer spend in 2025; GF says it would take an extended period to find a replacement and does not expect to acquire a significant amount of SOI wafers from alternate suppliers in the near term. In October 2024 GF executed an addendum to its 2017 MSA with Soitec for 300mm RFSOI and FD products, establishing the required supply volumes, pricing and other terms until 2026 and, subject to certain conditions, until 2030. Soitec is the largest of the principal silicon wafer suppliers with which GF has entered into multiple long-term agreements; GF notes Soitec relies on third-party providers for raw silicon wafers.
contracts.units: approximately 71% of GF SOI wafer spend (2025)
